title: By the fig and the olive, and the land they mark.
subtitle: Fruit that may point to a blessed place

row.title: the fruits
sub: the fig and olive you eat

then: Mujahid said it is {idea}this fig and olive that you have{/idea}. Others said the olive points to the Masjid of Jerusalem. Some imams said the fig and olive mark {idea}the land where Isa was sent{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ recited this surah while travelling.
now: You drizzle olive oil on bread or split a fig at breakfast. Simple, ancient food. {idea}The same fruits grow on hills where prophets walked.{/idea} Even your breakfast can carry you back to them.
old: A fig is just a fig.
new: These fruits are sworn by, and they point to a land of prophets.
try: Next time you eat an olive or a fig, say bismillah and remember the prophets of that land.

title: By Mount Sinai, where Allah spoke to Musa.
subtitle: The second place of great revelation
then: Ka'b Al-Ahbar and others said it is {idea}the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says Allah swore by a noble place, {reward}then a nobler, then the noblest of all{/reward}.
now: There are places in your life where something changed: the mosque where you first prayed properly, the hospital where a child was born. {idea}Places hold memories of meeting Allah's mercy.{/idea}
new: Some places are honoured because Allah spoke or acted there.
try: Think of one place where you felt close to Allah, and make a short dua for it.

title: And by this secure city, Makkah.
subtitle: The noblest of the three places
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others agreed: {idea}this city of security is Makkah{/idea}. There is no difference of opinion about it. It is where whoever enters is safe, and {reward}where Muhammad ﷺ was sent{/reward}.
now: You watch the live stream of the Kaaba on your phone at midnight, people circling in every hour. {reward}A city made safe by Allah.{/reward} You can carry a little of that safety by being a safe person for others.
old: Safety depends on locks and walls.
new: Allah can make a place safe, and asks me to be safe for others.
try: Make sure one person around you today feels completely safe with you.

title: You were made in the best form.
subtitle: What the three oaths were about
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}Allah created man in the best image and form, standing upright with straight limbs that He beautified{/reward}. The introduction notes the oath is by places of prophets, because {idea}human nature can reach as high as prophethood{/idea}.
now: You catch yourself in the bathroom mirror and pick at everything: the nose, the skin, the weight. {reward}Allah describes your making as the best form.{/reward} The criticism in your head is not His view.
old: There is so much wrong with how I look and who I am.
new: I was made in the best form, with room to rise very high.
try: Look in the mirror today and say alhamdulillah once, without adding a complaint.

title: Then the same person can fall to the lowest.
subtitle: From the best form to the lowest of the low
then: Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said this refers to the Fire, {trap}if they disobey Allah and deny the messengers{/trap}. Ibn Abbas also said it can mean frail old age, but Ibn Kathir prefers the first view, like {idea}man is in loss, except those who believe{/idea}.
now: Someone with every gift, the looks, the brains, the family, can still end up cruel and empty. {trap}A good start does not guarantee a good end.{/trap} {idea}The verse puts the turning point in your choices.{/idea}
old: I was born with good qualities, so I will be fine.
new: A beautiful start can still fall; what I do with it decides.
try: Ask yourself today: what is one gift Allah gave me that I am wasting?

title: Except those who believe and do good: an endless reward.
subtitle: The way out of the fall
then: Ibn Kathir says the reward here is {reward}one that will not end{/reward}. Those who believe and do righteous deeds are taken out of the fall. {idea}Faith and action, side by side.{/idea}
now: Your salary stops when you leave the job. Your phone dies when you forget to charge it. {reward}This reward is described as never cut off.{/reward} It starts with something as small as a kind word today.
old: Good things in life always run out.
new: Belief and good deeds earn a reward that never runs out.
try: Do one good deed today and pair it with a quiet act of faith, like a dhikr.

title: After all this, what makes you deny the Judgment?
subtitle: A question put straight to the reader
then: Ibn Kathir says this addresses every {idea}son of Adam{/idea}. You know the beginning, and {idea}He who began creation can repeat it, which is easier{/idea}. So what makes you deny the final return?
now: You plan your career for years ahead and never plan for the one appointment that is certain. {idea}The verse turns to you directly and asks why.{/idea} Not to shame you. To wake you.
old: The Day of Judgment feels too far off to think about.
new: The One who made me once can easily bring me back, so the Day is real.
try: Spend two minutes today thinking about meeting Allah, then do one thing to prepare.

title: Is Allah not the most just of judges?
subtitle: Why a Judgment Day must come
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}is He not the best of judges, who does not oppress anyone?{/idea} From His justice, he says, is that {reward}He will give retribution to the one who was wronged against whoever wronged him{/reward}.
now: Someone cheated you out of money, or spread a lie, and nothing happened to them. It eats at you. {reward}The case is not closed.{/reward} {idea}Allah is the Judge, and He also sees what you did to others.{/idea}
old: Some wrongs will never be made right.
new: The most just Judge will settle every wrong, including mine.
try: Think of anyone you may have wronged, and make it right or ask their forgiveness this week.
